object_description: three interlocking volumes stepped from six to four storeys
design_condition: The ensemble distributes the program among the existing buildings, perimeter basement levels, and a lower new pavilion on the square, preserving the existing building’s presence and enclosing a publicly accessible courtyard.

positive.statement: The ensemble fits well into the scale of the urban-development context.

position.rationale: Stepped interlocking bodies visibly moderate their combined scale across the sampled mass.

positive.statement: The three interlinked bodies form a skilfully designed and harmonious group.

position.rationale: The top plan and stepped elevations clearly show three overlapping volumes.

positive.statement: The new building achieves a reserved yet self-confident appearance on the public square.

position.target: new building on the public square
position.rationale: The lower eastern/southern portion reads as the reserved pavilion-facing public-square edge.

positive.statement: The intertwined bodies enclose a publicly accessible courtyard with pleasant proportions and an intimate character.

position.rationale: The interlocking plan leaves a recognizable central open gap between the sampled bodies.

positive.statement: The project shows great care and meets contemporary monument-preservation requirements.

position.rationale: Preservation relates to the retained northern-western edge, though historic elements are not distinguishable.

positive.statement: The structure, building technology, fire protection, and sustainability concepts provide a solid basis.

position.target: structure, building technology, fire protection, and sustainability concepts
position.rationale: These systems are evaluated globally without identifiable geometric markers.

negative.statement: The additional façade floors would benefit from cautious differentiation to clarify the sequence of historical periods.

position.rationale: Stepped facade bands are most apparent along the taller eastern and southern elevations.

negative.statement: The horizontal distribution level fulfils its role only to a limited extent, and the path connections are complicated and unclear.

position.rationale: The middle horizontal break is clearly visible across multiple stepped elevations.

negative.statement: The event, exhibition, and media rooms depend entirely on artificial light.

position.rationale: Interior uses are unshown; the marker samples the lower eastern volume.

negative.statement: The separation between children’s and adult libraries should be clearer to prevent noise nuisance.

position.rationale: Separate library zones are not visible; the anchor uses the central interlocking region.

negative.statement: Delivery works only to a limited extent, while administration requires long employee routes.

position.rationale: Service and administration are not identifiable; the eastern perimeter is the plausible access-side anchor.

negative.statement: Barrier-free objectives are achieved only partially.

position.rationale: Accessibility performance has no specific visible geometric referent.
